summary: State 6c518e7f4aa338a1 is the earlier session's hand-written body (172e4fb8c0ee2e5a: scalar tile base + 32-bit lane offsets, mask-free fast path, 4 v_fmac, DPP wave reduction; 114 instructions against amdclang's 157) launched with a 40 KB LDS reservation per workgroup instead of the 32 bytes the code uses. It measures 1.035 (CI 1.029..1.041) and 1.051 (1.043..1.056) over the baseline at 240 pairs, and 1.043 (1.041..1.048) head to head against the same code without the reservation; the body alone is parity (0.992), so the whole gain is the launch-level reservation. The kernel is at the memory floor (headroom 0.95 to 0.99, each element read once), so 1.5x is out of reach. Outputs are not bit-identical to the original binary (19 of 50 cases identical, max rel err 0.013 on large_exponent/seed0[N=40000]) but within the manifest tolerance in all 50 cases. No source state was made this session.

Occupancy throttle by registers: v_mov_b32 v140, 0 so a wave needs 144 VGPRs (3 waves per SIMD)
Reversed traversal: workgroup id b -> gridDim-1-b for reads and the workspace index

friction: check's `resources.lds_bytes` stays 32 for every relaunch with a larger `lds` (6c518e7f4aa338a1, 18b744a11d6f855a, ...), although the timings show the reservation is in effect (80 KB: 0.87). I could not confirm from any tool what the descriptor actually requests, nor how many workgroups per CU result; features/check should report the launched LDS size and the resulting workgroups-per-CU limit.

The mechanism of the 40 KB effect cannot be observed: there is no tool that reports resident waves or workgroups per CU, so 'which limit is active' is inferred from timings. The response is not monotone (20 KB 1.00, 26.5 KB 1.00, 32.5 KB 1.016, 40 KB 1.035-1.051, 45 KB 1.036, 52.5 KB 0.974, 80 KB 0.87) and 45 KB and 52.5 KB should both give 3 workgroups per CU by lds_per_cu / lds, yet differ by 6 %; the allocation granule or the real per-CU LDS pool is not what arch('resources') suggests.

The reference time floats between 135 and 141 us from one bench call to the next, so separate benches of close candidates rank unreliably (the 40 KB state measured 1.034, 1.051, 1.035); only compare() was stable (CI width 0.7 %). A sweep tool that times several relaunch values in one interleaved process would have made the LDS sweep cheaper and cleaner.
A 2D/3D grid (another dispatch order) could not be tried at the machine level: nothing says whether edit_ir enables the Y workgroup id register when the launch has a second grid dimension.

Kernarg preload into SGPRs (arch lists kernarg_preload_max_sgprs: 16) has no visible way to be enabled from edit_ir or relaunch; it would let the loads be issued without the s_load + s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0) prefix.
lessons: An LDS reservation larger than the code needs is a launch-level lever on a memory-bound reduction: rb_dot, 32768 workgroups of 512 threads, each reading 16 KB: lds=40960 gave 1.035 to 1.051 over the strongest amdclang build (240 pairs, three timings) and 1.043 (CI 1.041..1.048) in a direct compare against the same code with lds 32 bytes. On amdclang's own code the same relaunch gave 1.016 (1.011..1.019).

The LDS response is narrow and not monotone: 20 KB 1.002, 26.5 KB 0.996, 32.5 KB 1.016, 40 KB 1.035-1.051, 45 KB 1.036, 52.5 KB 0.974, 80 KB 0.868. Sweep 32 to 48 KB; above 50 KB it turns into a loss.

With the 40 KB reservation the block size stopped mattering on rb_dot: block 256 went from 0.945 to 1.039, block 128 from 0.935 to 1.028, block 64 from 0.983 to 1.027, block 512 from 0.992 to 1.035-1.051; block 256 against block 512 at 40 KB compares 1.003. The earlier losses of fewer, longer waves were about how many workgroups a CU holds at once, not about bytes per wave. Smaller reservations on those bodies did not help (block 256 at 20 KB 0.982, block 64 at 20 KB 0.991, at 10 KB 0.939).
Throttling occupancy through registers is not the same lever: a dead write to v140 (144 VGPRs, 3 waves per SIMD) on the same body measured 0.950.
Reversed workgroup traversal on rb_dot is parity (1.0007), as on rb_axpy.
Separate bench calls drift by 1 to 2 % in the reference (135 to 141 us here); rank candidates within 2 % of each other with compare(a, b, pairs=240) only.

session.final:
`rb_dot` now has its first verified win: state `6c518e7f4aa338a1` runs 1.035x to 1.051x faster than the strongest amdclang build, far short of the 1.5x target. The kernel sits at the memory floor (headroom 0.95 to 0.99, each element read once), so 1.5x is out of reach.

- **What the win is:** the earlier session's hand-written body, unchanged, launched with a 40 KB LDS reservation per workgroup instead of the 32 bytes the code uses. The body alone is parity (0.992), so the whole gain is the launch setting.
- **How firm it is:** three timings against the baseline gave 1.034 (60 pairs), 1.051 and 1.035 (240 pairs each). A direct comparison against the same code without the reservation gave 1.043 (CI 1.041 to 1.048).
- **Equivalence:** outputs are not bit-identical to the original binary (19 of 50 cases identical) but within the manifest tolerance in all 50.
- **Mechanism not established:** I read it as a cap on workgroups resident per compute unit, but the tools could not confirm that. The response is not monotone, and `check` reports `lds_bytes: 32` for every one of these states.

| LDS per workgroup | Speedup over baseline (240 pairs) |
|---|---|
| 20 KB | 1.002 |
| 26.5 KB | 0.996 |
| 32.5 KB | 1.016 |
| 40 KB | 1.035 to 1.051 |
| 45 KB | 1.036 |
| 52.5 KB | 0.974 |
| 80 KB | 0.868 |

Other things measured this session:

- **Block size stops mattering with the reservation:** the block 256, 128 and 64 bodies that lost before (0.945, 0.935, 0.983) all land at 1.03 to 1.04 with 40 KB. Those three are 60-pair triage timings; block 256 against block 512 at 40 KB compares 1.003 at 240 pairs.
- **amdclang's own code with 40 KB:** 1.016 (CI 1.011 to 1.019).
- **Throttling through register count** (a dead write to `v140`, 3 waves per SIMD): loss, 0.950.
- **Reversed workgroup traversal:** parity, 1.001.
